title: binscatter
summary: Visualize point density with a two-dimensional binned scatter plot.
description: `binscatter(x,y)` bins paired observations and displays the bin counts as a colored tile plot. `binscatter(x,y,nbins)` accepts a scalar or two-element bin count. `binscatter(tbl,xvar,yvar)` reads numeric variables from a table or timetable. Name-value options support `NumBins`, `XLimits`, `YLimits`, `ShowEmptyBins`, `FaceAlpha`, `DisplayName`, and `DisplayStyle` set to `"tile"`.
notes: Default bin counts use Scott-rule estimates capped at 100 bins per dimension. Explicit `NumBins` entries must be positive integers no greater than 250.

Real X/Y vectors, `NumBins`, and explicit `XLimits`/`YLimits` accept every built-in integer class. Integer X/Y data and explicit limits retain their native class and exact values in chart state; bin membership is computed exactly before floating bin-edge rendering, including across the full `uint64` range.

The returned handle has type `binscatter` and exposes `Values`, `XData`, `YData`, `NumBins`, `XBinEdges`, `YBinEdges`, `XLimits`, `YLimits`, `ShowEmptyBins`, `FaceAlpha`, and `DisplayName` through `get`.
`set` supports recomputing the chart after updates to `NumBins`, `ShowEmptyBins`, `XLimits`, `YLimits`, `XData`, `YData`, `FaceAlpha`, and `DisplayName`.
Empty bins are hidden from the rendered tile surface by default and are shown when `ShowEmptyBins` is true. The `Values` property preserves the numeric bin values either way.
RunMat renders `binscatter` as an indexed image surface with a colorbar. MATLAB's interactive chart UI affordances are not modeled.

Resident GPU-array input is a RunMat-only gather extension because the public `binscatter` extended-capability surface does not document GPU arrays. MATLAB-compatible mode rejects resident input before provider access.
